To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) passive states in AdS are characterized by a universal temperature, (2) passive states in two-dimensional AdS are necessarily pure, and (3) passive states in n-dimensional AdS induce a geodesic causal structure and satisfy strong independence conditions.

the stability properties of passive states for uniformly accelerated observers are sufficient to induce a geodesic causal structure and to guarantee a local, covariant, net of observables in any n-dimensional (n≥2) AdS space–time.

(a) the stability of the quantum state in the Unruh vacuum implies a PCT symmetry for uniformly accelerated observers, (b) the stability of this state implies the existence of a geodesic causal structure in AdS, and (c), the stability of the state implies the existence and uniqueness of a local net of observables indexed by wedge-shaped regions in AdS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: What are the properties of stable quantum systems in anti–de Siter (Ads) space?
the question: What are the implications for a theory of quantum gravity if it is to have a local causal structure in a curved space–time background?
the question of whether the properties of stable, local, covantiant quantum systems in AdS space are determined by the properties of the space–time geometry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the causal structure of AdS, its PCT symmetry, the existence of a universal Unruh temperature, and the independence of observables in complementary wedges are all consequences of the existence of passive states.

the passive states are the unique states which are stable under the action of all local observables, which are passive for uniformly accelerated AdS observers, and which are compatible with a weak localization of the theory.

the existence of a stable, passive state in AdS is equivalent to the existence of a geodesic causal structure, a universal value of Unruh temperature, PCT symmetry, a net of observables indexed by wedge-shaped regions, and a local, covariant, nontrivial, independent net of observables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the existence of a passive state for uniformly accelerated observers is equivalent to a number of properties that are characteristic for a quantum theory of gravity.
a passive state in AdS induces a causal structure, a local net of observables, a PCT symmetry and the Unruh effect.
the causal structure of AdS space–times, the independence properties of observables, and the spectral properties of local quantum systems are closely related.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the stability of quantum systems in AdS space–time implies a universal causal structure, which is compatible with PCT and with the independence of observables in complementary wedges, and that these properties are sufficient to construct a nontrivial net of local observables in two-dimensional AdS.
the causal structure of the state space in a theory of local quantum fields in AdS can be derived from the stability properties of passive states in AdS.
the existence of a passive state in n⩾2-dimensional AdS space–time is equivalent to a number of nontrivial properties of the theory.
